title: WHAT'S INSIDE A SINGLE DROP OF SEAWATER
subject: science

contradiction.viewer_thinks: seawater is just salty water — a drop is chemically simple and mostly empty
contradiction.actually: a single drop is a crowded ecosystem: tens of thousands of bacteria and hundreds of thousands of viruses

beats.narration: This is one drop of seawater. To your eye it is nothing — salt and wet. But it holds tens of thousands of bacteria and hundreds of thousands of viruses. It is a city in suspension.
beats.claim: a standard drop of surface seawater carries on the order of tens of thousands of bacteria and hundreds of thousands of viruses
beats.visual_question: what is actually inside one drop?
beats.visual_answer: a droplet silhouetted on the sea surface, its interior crowded with glowing specks no eye can see

beats.narration: By volume, a drop is mostly water and about three and a half percent salt — sodium and chloride, torn apart into ions. But the salt is not the surprise.
beats.claim: average ocean salinity is about 3.5%, dominated by sodium and chloride ions
beats.visual_question: what is the drop made of, by volume?
beats.visual_answer: a composition bar: water mass, salt ions split apart, and a thin living sliver highlighted at the end

beats.narration: Descend with the scale. At a tenth of a millimetre, the drop's architects appear: diatoms — drifting glass shells that harvest sunlight and make roughly a fifth of the food in the sea.
beats.claim: diatoms, glass-shelled single-celled algae, produce roughly a fifth of global photosynthetic production
beats.visual_question: what lives at the drop's largest scale?
beats.visual_answer: a diatom in engraved detail: a geometric glass shell with sunlight beams crossing it

beats.narration: Ten times smaller: bacteria, about a micrometre — the ocean's dominant engineers. And ten times smaller still, their constant companion: viruses, which burst cells daily and leak the carbon back into the water.
beats.claim: marine viruses repeatedly lyse bacteria, redirecting a substantial share of microbial biomass into dissolved organic matter
beats.visual_question: what happens between bacteria and viruses?
beats.visual_answer: a bacterium beside a swarm of smaller viruses; one cell bursts, its contents dissolving outward

beats.narration: Those leaking molecules do not vanish. They feed the bacteria, the bacteria feed everything that swims — the drop is where the ocean's food web actually begins.
beats.claim: the viral shunt's dissolved carbon feeds microbes that anchor the marine food web
beats.visual_question: where does the leaked carbon go?
beats.visual_answer: arrows climb the ladder: molecules to bacteria, bacteria up through grazers to fish larvae

beats.narration: Descend once more. Below the life, the chemistry: salt ions, dissolved gasses, a haze of organic molecules — a millionfold smaller than the bacteria, and just as busy.
beats.claim: the drop's smallest inhabitants — ions and dissolved molecules — operate at sub-nanometre scale, a millionfold below bacteria
beats.visual_question: what is left at the very bottom of the scale?
beats.visual_answer: the molecular floor: sodium and chloride ions drifting among dissolved gasses and organic specks

beats.narration: So the drop was never empty. One ladder of scale, one connected machine — and every glass of the ocean carries it: the city in suspension.
beats.claim: a drop of seawater is a connected multi-scale ecosystem, from molecules to algae
beats.visual_answer: the full scale ladder resolved in one frame: drop, diatom, bacterium, virus, ion — one glowing chain

visual_contradiction.seems: a drop of seawater is chemically simple — salty water and nothing more
visual_contradiction.actually: it is a crowded ecosystem spanning a millionfold range of scale, from glass-shelled algae to ions
visual_contradiction.reveal: the descent reveals the crowded interior: specks resolve into diatom, bacteria, viruses, then molecules

payoff_image.image: the resolved scale ladder in one frame — drop, diatom, bacterium, virus, ion linked by a single glowing line
